books.section: The Rise of the Service Sector

stimulus.source_note: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Population Survey.
stimulus.text:
| Sector | 1983 | 2010 |
| Private-sector workers in unions | 16.8% | 6.9% |
| Public-sector workers in unions | 36.7% | 36.2% |

Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Population Survey. Simplified for this test.

parts.prompt: Identify one thing the table shows about union membership between 1983 and 2010.
parts.modelAnswer: The table shows private-sector union membership collapsing, from 16.8 percent of private-sector workers in 1983 to 6.9 percent in 2010. Public-sector membership, by contrast, held almost steady near 36 percent.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for identifying one thing the table shows, such as the sharp fall in private-sector membership or the stability of public-sector membership.
scoring.notEarned: Naming a figure with no comparison, or stating something the table does not show, does not earn the point.

parts.prompt: Briefly explain ONE reason private-sector union membership fell as the table shows.
parts.modelAnswer: Factory jobs were the most unionized private-sector jobs, and they shrank for decades as firms automated and moved production abroad. Service work grew to replace them, and service jobs were far less unionized.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for explaining one reason, such as the shrinkage of manufacturing, offshoring, automation, or the growth of less-unionized service work.
scoring.notEarned: Naming a reason with no explanation, or explaining the public-sector figures instead, does not earn the point.

parts.prompt: Briefly explain ONE consequence of the decline in private-sector union membership.
parts.modelAnswer: With fewer workers bargaining together, workers had less power to press for higher pay, and economists link the union decline to wage stagnation for workers without a college degree. Inequality widened as bargaining power thinned.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for explaining one consequence, such as weaker bargaining power, wage stagnation, or widening inequality.
scoring.notEarned: Naming a consequence with no explanation, or describing a consequence for the public sector, does not earn the point.
